newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Shenzhen bourse to speed up price reports.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen bourse to speed up price reports.

text.p: In a move described as a great leap forward for fair trading in China, Shenzhen stock exchange will boost the speed at which it transmits domestic stock prices to investors.

The Shenzhen Securities Satellite Communication Co Ltd, partly owned by the exchange, signed a deal on Friday to buy a system that will provide investors with price information at almost real-time speed, a company official told Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin on Monday.
The system, costing 20-30 million yuan ($2.4-3.6 million), is designed by WavePhore Inc, and made and sold by U.S.-based Oregon Manufacturing Services Inc, he said.
The new system will transmit information at a speed of 256 kbps, compared with 19.2 kbps now, reducing the current delay of several seconds to almost nothing, the official said.
"This is a big leap for fair trading," another official said.

"The stock market is moving all the time and if someone misses a moment they can lose money," he said, adding that investors had complained about the current speed that price information reached them.
The system will begin operating in the first half of 1997, officials said but did not elaborate.
Shenzhen Electronics Group Import and Export Corp, a 100 percent-owned subsidiary of Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd, was the importer, the company officials said.
OMS and WavePhore officials were not immediately available for comment.
